## Amendment — the diagnosis here was only half the story (#3504)

This issue concluded that the lifecycle gates are blind to **unscoped** work: an issue with no xBRIEF contributes no origin, so `verify:completed-tracked` skips it and reports green. That remains true and is still worth fixing.

But it was not the only reason tonight's five fixes had no briefs.

**`.git/info/exclude` on the maintainer clone contains a bare `xbrief/active/` line** (#3504). Every xBRIEF created in `active/` on that machine is invisible to git — `git add -A` skips it silently, `git status` never shows it. So even a correct parent workflow that *did* create briefs would have produced untracked ones there.

```
$ git check-ignore -v xbrief/active/2026-08-19-3502-....xbrief.json
.git/info/exclude:33:xbrief/active/	xbrief/active/2026-08-19-3502-....xbrief.json
```

Observed directly while committing the #3502 PR: the brief was silently dropped from `git add -A`. It is also why the #3476 brief "was never tracked on master" — it could not be.

### What this changes

There are **two** independent failure paths to landed-work-without-a-brief, and this issue only covers the first:

1. **No brief was ever created** — the process gap this issue describes. Detector: closed issue + merged PR + no origin anywhere.
2. **A brief was created but git cannot see it** — a clone-configuration gap. Detector: lifecycle roots hidden by `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` / `core.excludesFile` / `skip-worktree`. Filed separately as **#3505**.

A detector for (1) alone would still have reported clean on this machine for any brief that *was* created, because the artifact never became trackable. The two need to ship together, or (1) inherits a blind spot it cannot see.

### Also relevant to this issue's acceptance

The acceptance here says the five issues in the table must be detected when run against this session's range. That validation has to happen on a clone where lifecycle roots are visible — otherwise a passing run proves nothing about the detector.

Policy recorded as a decision: `xbrief/decisions/2026-08-19-lifecycle-artifacts-under-xbrief-are-shared-tracked-repository-s.decision.json` — lifecycle artifacts are shared tracked state; no per-clone ignore mechanism may hide a lifecycle root. Evidence: 406 commits have touched `xbrief/active/*` across 543 distinct brief paths.

Refs #3504, #3505
UAT Tester 6 adds sibling cases: change-request closed by comment with no xBRIEF, and a brief stuck in active after the GitHub issue merged. Details: #4703
Follow-up: #4703 is split and closed. The comment-close / no-xBRIEF remainder is now #4713. #3495 stays the merged-PR unscoped path.

Round 1, fresh open critique. Input ceiling: 5955184191. Evidence pin: f2a0930a0a5aa81a0b07d90980f921b8c1dea8cb. Verification method: read-only `git show <dispatch-sha>:` and pinned source searches; no runtime tests or DCR rerun. I read the body and comments through the ceiling, not later sibling posts.

The detection gap warrants work. The design should add bounded discovery of merged-close issues while preserving the existing named-issue land check. Before binding, resolve what counts as durable origin evidence and what proves that a merged PR actually closed the issue.

### 1. The missing capability is discovery, not all no-origin detection — sharpens-framing

Evidence: [completed-tracked lines 771–803](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/f2a0930a0a5aa81a0b07d90980f921b8c1dea8cb/packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts#L771-L803) synthesize an origin for `--issue N` when none exists. [The existing regression at line 487](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/f2a0930a0a5aa81a0b07d90980f921b8c1dea8cb/packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-tracked-on-delivery.test.ts#L487) explicitly covers closed, unlanded, no-local-origin input. Conversely, the corpus path builds its subjects from artifacts and returns success for zero origins (lines 726–828). Orphan-active starts with `listActiveRunningBriefs` (evaluate.ts:578).

Failure mode: reading P1's “never subjects” literally obscures the existing protection and invites weakening a fail-closed DONE check into a warn-only detector. Consequence: narrow the warrant to automatic corpus discovery. Preserve named-issue behavior. Prefer a sibling discovery verb sharing identity/artifact utilities; an explicit discovery mode on the existing verb is also viable if its defaults and exits remain backward-compatible.

### 2. Local presence cannot certify shared lifecycle coverage — blocks-the-design

Evidence: [local scan lines 351–374](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/f2a0930a0a5aa81a0b07d90980f921b8c1dea8cb/packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts#L351-L374) reads filesystem artifacts; the current verifier separately checks delivery-tip blobs. Amendment 5344624382 records the ignored-artifact failure path. Stop 1 still proposes “no origin in any lifecycle folder” without naming whose tree.

Failure mode: worker A has an ignored/uncommitted brief and suppresses the warning; clean worker B reports the same merged issue. A shared-state check becomes clone-dependent. A pending tracked origin also proves scoping, not completed land.

Consequence: define the inverse detector against parsed, repository-qualified origins in tracked lifecycle artifacts at one resolved delivery SHA. Report local-only evidence separately; it must not certify shared coverage. Keep terminal-land debt with completed-tracked. Reuse its identity parsing and legacy-layout support, not filenames or incidental issue mentions. This makes P1 independent of whether an agent happened to retain scratch files.

### 3. Merged association is not proof of closure — blocks-the-design

Evidence: the issue acceptance requires the *closing* PR to be merged; comments 5716667268 and 5717900755 expressly separate comment-close into #4713. The inspected completed-tracked evaluator resolves issue state, not closing-PR causality.

Failure mode: issue references a merged PR, then is manually closed as duplicate or not planned. A “closed + any linked merged PR” implementation incorrectly absorbs #4713 and reports unscoped delivery. Reopened issues and multiple linked PRs add the same ambiguity.

Consequence: specify authoritative closure-event/closing-PR evidence, repository identity, and current closed state as the discovery predicate. Add negative fixtures for merely linked PRs, unmerged closers, and reopened issues. Unavailable or incomplete forge evidence is an incomplete scan, not zero findings; warn-first must not turn authentication or pagination failure into a clean verdict.

### 4. P2 should require explicit exemption decisions, not blanket bot immunity — sharpens-framing

Evidence: Stop 1 lists bot authors, chores, docs, and reverts as legitimate-unscoped classes while leaving the axis open. None of those properties establishes that work was trivial: an automation account can implement a substantial fix, and a revert can change significant behavior.

Failure mode: exempting all bot authors recreates P1 specifically for automated work. Inferring scope from titles, prose, or diff size lets untrusted or lossy metadata decide whether lifecycle obligations apply.

Consequence: prefer an exact, project-configured exemption label/rule with visible excluded counts and reasons; default unknown classes to reported, not exempt. The strongest alternative is automatic Dependabot exclusion for low-noise adoption. It would win if constrained to a documented dependency-update identity/type conjunction with counterexample tests, rather than author alone. P2 can be satisfied by explicitly marking legitimate chores/docs/reverts; no semantic “triviality” classifier is needed.

### 5. Pin both the discovery interval and artifact snapshot — sharpens-framing

Evidence: acceptance demands detection of five historical issues before backfill, then clean results after backfill. The existing [delivery-tip resolver](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/f2a0930a0a5aa81a0b07d90980f921b8c1dea8cb/packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts#L389-L419) already separates the checked tip from feature HEAD.

Failure mode: an old date range paired with today's artifacts hides the original five. “Since latest tag” can also choose a tag that was not a release, or leave first-release consumers undefined.

Consequence: preserve P3's standalone placement, default warnings, and opt-in enforcement. Choose one documented finite default interval with explicit since/until overrides; print the resolved UTC boundaries and artifact SHA. Freeze forge evidence plus pre-backfill artifact state for the five-case regression, with a separate post-backfill control. Paginate completely within that interval. Report candidate, exempt, missing, and unresolved counts. A days-based default is simpler than release-tag inference; release preflight can supply explicit bounds.

### 6. DCR must follow behavior without dictating the command name — sharpens-framing

Evidence: comment 5944829546 identifies one harness predicate, `forge.completed_tracked_reports_unscoped_merged_close`, and its observed old-command zero-origin success. I have not independently reproduced that pack.

Failure mode: a correct sibling detector leaves a harness that still invokes only completed-tracked red; renaming the predicate alone proves nothing.

Consequence: retain R.3495 traceability, update the harness invocation/assertions alongside the chosen public surface, and assert named missing issues under default warning mode plus nonzero debt under enforcement. Keep the old named-issue regression. The source re-derivation supports the gap; the historical DCR output remains reported evidence, not a new measurement by this critic.

Pain coverage of this critique: P1 is addressed by findings 1–3 and 5; P2 by 4; P3 by 1, 3, 5, and 6. Panel-deposit matches the envelope ceiling and SHA; sibling completion is not observable within this envelope.

Critic exit after this single post.

## Verdict

Stop 1 warrant holds. Pin-read at `f2a0930a0a5a` shows `evaluateCompletedTracked` builds subjects only from lifecycle xBRIEF origins (`scanLocalOrigins` over `LOCAL_ORIGIN_FOLDERS` plus tip nonterminal brief blobs). Empty `originMap` exits 0 with `scanned N briefs, resolved 0 origins; nothing to check.` That is exactly the inverse-blind green DCR R.3495 reports. `verify:orphan-active` enumerates only `active/` running briefs (`listActiveRunningBriefs`), so a never-briefed merged close is also invisible there. Mechanism-shaped clearance and the three-pain denominator are sound for an open-critique Bound.

## P1 — origin-driven blindness

**Take:** accept as the primary pain. Re-verified anchors:

- `packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts` ~L39–46 `LOCAL_ORIGIN_FOLDERS`; ~L328–377 `scanLocalOrigins`; ~L805–828 empty-origin green path; header rule is closed **scoped** issues with a known origin.
- `packages/core/src/orphan-active/running-briefs.ts` ~L34–67 active/running-only subject set.
- `tasks/verify.yml` completed-tracked desc still says "Closed scoped GitHub issues with a known lifecycle xBRIEF origin".
- Consumer composition pin keeps completed-tracked **off** `check:consumer` (`consumer_check_gate_integrity.test.ts`); orphan-active stays on the merge chokepoint in candidate-scoped form.

Failure mode if unmet: cohort-close / release pre-flight keep printing green while unscoped merged closes accumulate — the OP five-issue table and DCR `forge.completed_tracked_reports_unscoped_merged_close` class.

`--issue N` synthesis when no local brief (#3476 drive-to DONE) is **not** the inverse sweep; it only proves a named origin. Do not mistake that path for P1 relief.

The one in-tree predicate shaped for this, `isAppActor` (`packages/core/src/one-pr-unit/close-via-app.ts:46-49`), has **zero callers at the pin** — a repo-wide grep at the dispatch sha returns the definition line and nothing else, not even its own test file.

And the field a builder would reach for first does not work. `closed_by` is read nowhere in the tree, and the typed close-evidence path drops it: `IssueStatePayload` is state plus stateReason (`completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts:170-173`) and `payloadFromRaw` populates from `raw.state` and `raw.state_reason` only (`:181-188`). **Failure mode.** A builder handed P1 and P3 has a policy with no measurement, and two branches, both bad. This is the same shape as the finding that cost the last round: a classification asserted as discharging a boundary, where the named mechanism verifiably does not look at the axis the boundary is drawn on. ### B2 — `blocks-the-design` — P1/P3: the facet enum has no slot for "evidence unavailable", so the enforce channel fails open on every forge-evidence failure, including the documented offline path

**Evidence.** P1 states that incomplete forge evidence resolves unresolved and that incomplete is not clean. P3 states a three-member closed facet set: `merged-closing-pr`, `app-claimed-origin`, `none`. Those are two different axes. P1's unresolved state lives on the close-**kind** axis (shipped versus abandoned, from state and state_reason). The facet set is the close-**evidence** axis, and it has no unresolved member. Only the second axis gates enforce.

The in-tree primitives already preserve the distinction the enum discards. `fetchClosingIssuesReferences` returns null on gh-absent, timeout, nonzero exit, parse failure, and unexpected shape (`pr-protected-issues/gh.ts:101-139`), and null is distinguishable from an empty list. `finalize-cohort.ts:283-305` makes the opposite choice for `fetchIssueClosed` and carries an in-source comment explaining why it accepts that. The facet enum collapses both "evidence says no closing PR" and "could not obtain evidence" into `none`, which the ruling makes report-only.

The offline path is documented, not hypothetical. `content/commands.md:329`: under `--skip-gh`, a named `--issue` with no cached state fails closed, and the unscoped corpus scan keeps the offline allowance. The discovery mode rides that same verb and that same flag. The `.deft` issue cache is open-biased as well: every existing `restIssueListPaginated` call site in the tree passes state open (`triage/queue/reconcile-live-state.ts:31`, `triage/evaluate/github.ts:166` and `:184`, `triage/classify/withdraw.ts:176`, `value/feedback-file.ts:196`, `product-signal/github-private-sink-adapter.ts:155`), so a closed issue that triage never walked has no cached payload either.

**Failure mode.** Run the discovery mode with `--enforce --skip-gh` over a real window: no live leg, no facet evidence for any subject, every subject classified `none`, every subject printed report-only, exit 0. Same outcome on a gh auth failure, a rate-limit, or a token that cannot read PRs. The operator reads a candidate count, an exempt count of zero, and a report-only list, and nothing in that output separates "this window is clean under enforce" from "this run could not tell." P1's own sentence forbids exactly that, and P3's enum has nowhere to put it.

**Disposition consequence.** Either a fourth facet `unresolved`, or make close-evidence a two-field record so the ruling's debt set reads over the facet while the exit code reads over both. P3 also names the enforce exit for a nonzero unresolved count and the `--skip-gh` discovery behaviour. **This changes what a lean can harvest from P3.**

---

### B3 — `sharpens-framing` — P2: the held harvest lost "print exempt reasons/counts"; only the abandoned-closed count survived

**Injection / suppression lens, triggered.** The target decides what becomes invisible to a lifecycle gate, over forge-controlled input (state_reason, labels, milestone, author login) and tracked config. The lens applies, and this is the finding it produces.

**Evidence.** Recut 5955812025 bind item 5 and Bound-remedy item 5 both end with "print exempt reasons/counts". The Handoff's held-harvest list keeps ignores-only plus the `resolveScopeRules` prohibition and adds abandoned-closed-as-exempt-count as a candidate. P2 on this Stop 1 carries the abandoned-closed count and the ignores-only rule, and the exempt-reasons clause is gone. At the pin, `resolveScopeIgnores` suppresses on three axes (`scope-rules.ts:55-85`): a `label` per entry, a `milestone` per entry, and an author rule with an any-of list. The source is `plan.policy.triageScopeIgnores`, a list authored to quiet the triage **walk**.

**Failure mode.** One list now carries two meanings. An operator adds a bot login to `triageScopeIgnores` to stop triage noise and silently widens the set of shipped work that owes no brief. With a bare exempt count there is no number separating "abandoned-closed, printed" from "matched an ignore entry someone added last month for an unrelated reason," and no way to see which entry matched. I will not close this on a reviewer noticing the config diff; the deterministic control is reason attribution on the printed exempt line. The repair the Stop 1 did make — abandoned-closed as a named exempt count rather than a silent drop — is the right shape, and should extend to the other suppression axis rather than replace it.

**Disposition consequence.** P2 restores "print exempt reasons/counts" and requires each exempt subject to name the matched rule (abandoned-closed with its state_reason; ignore-by-author with the login; ignore-by-label with the name). One clause on P2. The carve-out mechanism itself does not change, so full coverage of P2 is still reachable.

---

### B4 — `sharpens-framing` — P3: the window anchor is reachability-derived, so the same verb at the same wall clock reports a different debt set from different checkouts

**Evidence.** P3 binds a window since the last annotated release tag with a 30-day fallback. The pin has two different resolvers in one module. `fromGit` runs `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` (`packages/core/src/platform/resolve-version.ts:104`), which selects the most recent tag **reachable from HEAD**, not the most recent release. `latestLocalPublishableTag` (`:117-129`) shells `git tag --list` and selects through `latestPublishableTag`, which is semver-ordered and checkout-independent. P3 names neither. Tags in this repo really are annotated objects — `git for-each-ref` over `refs/tags` reports objecttype tag — so the annotated qualifier is satisfiable. But a tag object carries a tagger date distinct from the tagged commit's committer date, and the window filters issue `closed_at`, which is a forge clock. P3 names none of those three.

**Failure mode.** This arc's own dest is a detached worktree. Run the discovery verb from a branch forked before the last release and `git describe` returns an older reachable tag, so the window starts earlier and the report is wider; run it from the delivery tip and it starts later. Two honest runs, same clock, different debt sets, no diagnostic. That is a determinism defect on an issue carrying the determinism label, and the 30-day fallback never fires because a tag did resolve: the failure is a wrong window, not a missing one. Pair this with the prior audit's footnote that `restIssueListPaginated` exposes no since parameter (`scm/gh-rest.ts:691-700`), which I re-verified. The window is a client-side filter on `closed_at`, so the anchor has to be converted to an explicit UTC instant.

**Disposition consequence.** P3 names the resolver (`latestPublishableTag` over the tag list, not `git describe`), names the date field it converts to, and states that a resolved-but-wrong anchor is not the same state as no anchor. The printed UTC bounds P3 already requires then become checkable against something. One clause on P3.

---

### B5 — `sharpens-framing` — P1: `restIssueListPaginated` names two different exported functions at the pin

**Evidence.** `packages/core/src/scm/gh-rest.ts:691` and `packages/core/src/cache/fetch.ts:320` both export a function of that name. They are near-twins with different seams: the scm one takes a third `GhRestSeams` argument and routes through `execApi`; the cache one takes `runGhApiFn` inside its options object, routes through `execListPage`, and is the module-level mutable lister seam (`cache/fetch.ts:157`, swapped by `setPaginatedLister`). P1 names the symbol bare.

**Failure mode.** A builder imports the cache twin. The discovery sweep then rides a seam that `setPaginatedLister` can replace at runtime and inherits the cache module's normalisation path rather than the scm layer's. Nothing fails; the sweep simply answers from a different seam than the one P1's bulk-enumerate reasoning was written against, and the test double covering one does not cover the other.

**Disposition consequence.** P1 qualifies the module. One token. Worth stating because P1's whole value on this point is use-this-function-not-that-one, and at the pin the name alone does not identify a function.

---

### B6 — `footnote` — a bounding limit truncates silently where the page cap throws

Both variants return a sliced list on reaching the options limit (`scm/gh-rest.ts:738-740`, `cache/fetch.ts:352`) with no truncation signal, while the pagination-cap path throws with a fail-closed hint. If the sweep passes a limit to bound cost at the cohort-close call site, a truncated scan is indistinguishable from a complete clean one. No separate disposition weight: B2's unresolved clause covers this if it is written over scan completeness and not only over per-subject evidence. Recorded so that clause gets written wide enough.

### B7 — `footnote` — the close-kind resolver's fail-closed polarity was tuned for a refuse, and the named-issue confirm path inherits it into a report

P1 correctly keeps `resolveIssueCloseKind` off the sweep; the Recut kept it for the named-issue confirm. Note for whoever writes that path: when the live leg fails it returns shipped-closed from a stale cache rather than unknown (`completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts:296-312`), because in its #5126 caller shipped-closed means refuse-the-cancel and that is the conservative direction. In a discovery report, shipped-closed means name-this-issue-as-debt, so the same conservative bias produces a false accusation from a stale cache instead of a safe refusal. The in-source comment documents the #5126 intent, so this is a reuse-polarity note, not a defect in that function.

The enumerator half has no named mechanism and the tree has none. - The generic paginator ends three ways: empty page (`gh-rest.ts:725-726`), short page (`:737`), cap throw (`:743-748`). Its fourth exit, the `limit` path, returns `out.slice(0, options.limit)` (`:734`) — truncation and completion are the same return value, with no field saying which happened. The completeness signal is "it did not throw."
- The one hand-rolled paginated **pulls** walk in the tree is `fetchPrFiles` (`packages/core/src/pr-closing-keywords/main.ts:105-148`): explicit page cursor, `for (let page = 1; page <= 30; ...)` (`:108`), `break` on empty page and on short page, and on exhausting all 30 pages it falls out of the loop and `return out` (`:147`). A silent truncate at its cap — in a function whose own comment (`:107`) records that the pagination exists so later briefs cannot bypass admission.

**Failure mode.** `P1` asserts "Incomplete/throw/page-cap -> unresolved fail-closed under enforce" in the same sentence as "**stop** once `updated_at` precedes window start". A builder implementing both writes two exits that mean opposite things — "the sort key proves nothing later can be in-window" and "I ran out of budget" — and neither existing shape carries that difference past the `return`. When they collapse, which is what both existing shapes do, the gate reports a complete scan it did not perform. The merged PRs past the break never contribute, their issues lose the `merged-closing-pr` origin, and they land in facet `none`, which the held ruling keeps report-only. Fail-open, silently, out of a clause written to be fail-closed.

Second leg, textual. The held Reject list refuses "Silent truncate of pulls/issues page lists under enforce." `P1`'s stop *is* a truncation of a pulls page list; what makes it legitimate is a proof, not the absence of a cap. Folded verbatim, the lean carries a Reject line and a bind clause that read as contradicting each other, and resolving that contradiction edits held text — which the narrow ruling does not obviously authorize, so the Stop 1 is where it has to be said.

**Disposition consequence.** Two clauses in `P1` and one recording line. State the stop as a completeness **proof** with a recorded outcome — the enumerator reports which of `window-exhausted`, `cap`, or `error` ended the walk, and only the first counts as a complete scan — and record on the Stop 1 that folding it *qualifies* the held Reject line rather than contradicting it. Neither touches the enumerator choice or the hybrid.

### C3 — `sharpens-framing` — "(sound because `updated_at` >= `merged_at`)" proves the stop, not the enumeration; `sort=updated` pagination can skip an unseen in-window merged PR, and the skip drains to a report-only facet

**Evidence.** The inequality is true, and it does exactly what `P1` says: a row whose `updated_at` precedes window start has `merged_at <= updated_at`, so it is out of window, and under `direction=desc` so is every row after it. That licenses the break. It does not license the claim that the rows *before* the break are all the rows.

`sort=updated&direction=desc` orders a **mutable** key across a paginated read. Any PR touched during the walk — a comment, a label, a bot, a backport push — moves toward page 1. A PR sitting on an unfetched page when the walk starts, and touched before the walk reaches it, has already moved behind the cursor and is never returned. The same shift re-serves a boundary row, so the observable symptom is a duplicate (harmless; dedupe by number) while the loss is silent. This is GitHub list-ordering semantics, not a pin cite, and I flag it as such; the consequence below is pinned.

**Failure mode.** A skipped merged PR is an issue that loses its `merged-closing-pr` origin. Held bind item 5 routes evidence-*unavailable* to `unresolved` — but a skip is not evidence unavailable, it is evidence never requested, so nothing in the matrix catches it and the issue falls to `none`, which the ruling keeps report-only. The run prints a complete scan, a smaller debt set, and zero unresolved. That is the suppression channel the prior audit's lens named, reached through the remedy rather than through the gap the remedy closed.

**Disposition consequence.** Drop the unqualified "sound because" and state the precondition the soundness actually rests on: the stop is sound **given a stable ordering across the walk**, and the gate records what it does when it cannot have one. One clause, at Bound altitude — it names a property, not a recipe.

**Road not taken.** I considered recommending `sort=created&direction=desc`, since creation order is immutable and pagination over it is stable. I did not: `created_at` can precede `merged_at` by an arbitrary interval, so a stop on `created_at` before window start loses rows — unsound in the exact direction `updated_at` was chosen to avoid. The genuinely stable alternative is the issues endpoint's `since`, which the held helper does not carry (C1), so naming it here would reopen C1's surface instead of this one.

**Steelman and what flips me.** The strongest rejected position: the skip window is seconds to minutes wide, the population is the handful of PRs merged in a release window, and a debt gate that loses one to a race is still enormously better than today's blindness. True, and it is why this is sharpening rather than blocking. What keeps it a finding is the word *sound* in `P1`. A Stop 1 that records soundness as settled takes the question out of the fold entirely — a builder reading it has no reason to think about ordering at all, and the failure is quiet on both ends. Replacing "sound because" with the precondition flips this to a footnote. So would one sentence naming ordering instability as accepted cost.

---

### C4 — `blocks-the-design` — P2 inverts the resolved-tag-with-empty-date path; both in-tree tag-list readers collapse *unreadable* and *absent* into one `null`, which routes to the same silent 30-day fallback, and the root rename P2 prescribes moves traffic into that hole

**Evidence** (`packages/core/src/platform/resolve-version.ts`, re-opened at the pin):

- `latestPublishableTag` is a pure selector over an iterable of names (`:33-44`), returns `null` when nothing publishable is found, and swallows comparison failures in a bare `catch {}` (`:42`).
- `latestLocalPublishableTag` (`:118-130`): `const cwd = repoRoot ?? frameworkRoot()` (`:119`) — the defect `P2` names — then `execFileSync("git", ["tag", "--list"], ...)` (`:121`) inside a `try` whose `catch` returns `null` (`:127`), feeding `latestPublishableTag(stdout.split("\n"))` (`:126`). There is no `payloadIsOwnGitRoot` guard here; that guard (`:86`) is used only by `fromGit` (`:101-102`).
- `latestRemotePublishableTag` (`:132-149`) carries the same `frameworkRoot()` default (`:139`), the same catch-to-`null` (`:147`), and takes a git **remote name**, not an owner/repo coordinate.

So four distinct states return the identical `null`: the root is not a git work tree; `git` is absent or times out; the checkout has no tags fetched; the repository genuinely has no publishable tag. `P2` makes a fifth state — tag resolved, dates empty — a failure, and leaves all four of those on "no-anchor, N=30d."

**Failure mode.** The third state is the common one and it is not exotic: a clone made without tags, the default shape of most CI checkouts, yields an empty tag list on a repository that has releases. The run then reports a 30-day window, prints "no anchor" truthfully, and emits a debt set computed over the wrong interval. That is W1's own failure mode verbatim — two honest runs, same clock, different debt sets — reached one step earlier in the same chain, on a path a builder is more likely to hit than the `frameworkRoot()` misroute `P2` does name.

Note also what fixing the named defect does on its own. The `frameworkRoot()` default at least pointed at a checkout that reliably has tags; repointing it at the inspected repository is correct, and it *increases* exposure to the unfetched-tags state. The repair `P2` prescribes moves traffic into the hole `P2` leaves open.

I will not close this on a builder remembering to fetch tags, and I will not close it on the operator reading the printed line. The deterministic control is the one `P2` already chose on the other path — make the unreadable state a failure rather than a fallback — and taking it requires a reader that can tell those states apart, which the two in-tree helpers cannot by construction.

**Disposition consequence.** `P2`'s failure clause covers the tag-list **read**, not only the date conversion: an unreadable tag list, or a project root that is not a git work tree, is a failure on the same footing as a resolved tag with empty dates. Only a *successfully read* tag list containing no publishable tag earns the N=30d no-anchor path. The print obligation picks up tag-list cardinality so the two stay distinguishable in the record afterwards. **This changes the pain text.** Folded as written, the lean would carry relief of a determinism defect that stays open on its likelier path.

**Steelman and what flips me.** The strongest rejected position: `P2` names its own root, so a correct implementation reads the right repository, and a checkout whose tags were never fetched is an operator environment problem rather than a design one — the Bound should not grow a clause for every way a checkout can be wrong. I take that seriously; it is the general shape of the reviewer-will-catch-it close, which is why I am naming a control instead of relying on attention. The control is cheap: the state is observable at the point of the read, and the fold already requires a print. One clause making the read failure a failure flips me. So would an explicit sentence recording empty-tag-list-on-a-releasing-repo as accepted cost, with the 30-day window named as the known-wrong answer it produces. What does not flip it is the root rename alone, which is the half `P2` currently has.

---

### C5 — `sharpens-framing` — P2 says "is failure" and names no channel; the held enforce matrix has no slot for a run-global failure, and the verb is warn-first

**Evidence.** Held bind item 6 fails closed on "`merged-closing-pr` plus nonzero unresolved/incomplete scan", and held Bound remedy item 1 prints one count across candidate / exempt-with-reason / missing-debt / report-only / unresolved. Every one of those is per-subject — an issue, or one PR's contribution. Window resolution is not per-subject: it fixes the denominator for the entire run. The prior audit's F2 already recorded that one `unresolved` number carries two different remedies (close-kind at item 4, close-evidence at item 5); `P2` adds a third condition with no stated home. Held item 9 also makes the verb warn-first by default, and "is failure" has no defined meaning under warn-default.

**Failure mode.** The builder's cheapest reading folds it into `unresolved`, where item 6 fails closed only under `--enforce` — so the warn-default run prints a debt list computed over an unanchored window with an `unresolved: 1` line beside it, and the list is the artifact people act on. The other faithful reading makes it a hard exit and breaks warn-first. Both are readings of the same sentence, which is the defect.

**Disposition consequence.** `P2` names the channel: run-global refusal in both warn and enforce, distinct from the per-subject `unresolved` count — or `unresolved` plus an explicit statement that warn-default still prints the list. One clause either way, and it does not touch the held matrix's shape.

---

### F1 — `footnote` — "the repository under inspection" has two live coordinates on the sibling verb, and P2 does not say which wins

The sibling gate carries both `--repo OWNER/NAME` (`packages/cli/src/verify-completed-tracked.ts:57`, default `null` at `:36`) and `--project-root` (default `"."` at `:35`, assigned at `:48-53`), resolves the latter at `:108`, and passes them into the evaluator independently (`:111-113`). Nothing ties them: `--repo deftai/directive --project-root /some/other/checkout` is accepted, and the issue denominator and the tag window then come from different repositories, both printed truthfully. `P2`'s phrase resolves the `frameworkRoot()` default but not this. No disposition weight — the fold is strictly better than the status quo on this axis either way, and the print obligation `P2` already carries makes a mismatch visible to a reader who looks for it. Recorded because "the repository under inspection" reads as unambiguous and on this verb's argv it is two things.

### F2 — `footnote` — the taggerdate-to-creatordate fallback changes clock, not just field

On `git for-each-ref refs/tags/<tag>`, `%(creatordate)` is the tag object's own date for an annotated tag and the tagged commit's committer date for a lightweight one. The fallback therefore answers "when was the release cut" on one tag type and "when was that commit written" on the other, and a long-lived branch merged and tagged later puts those days apart. The pain-audit established that this fallback is what makes a lightweight tag work at all, given that `latestPublishableTag` filters on semver publishability rather than on annotation, and it is right that it stays — I am not asking for a change. `P2` already requires printing the chosen date field, which is what makes the difference legible. Recorded so that whoever writes the print surface does not describe the two fields as one quantity measured twice.

---

**Injection / suppression lens, triggered.** The target decides what becomes invisible to a lifecycle gate, over forge-controlled input (`merged_at`, `updated_at`, closing references) and environment-controlled input (the checkout's refs). It fires, and it pays out twice — in both cases *through the remedy rather than through the original gap*. At C3 the enumerator's ordering key is mutable and noise-reachable: anything that touches a PR mid-walk can move it behind the cursor, and the lost row drains into facet `none`, which the ruling makes report-only, so a shortfall does not merely lose precision, it silently exempts. At C4 the channel is checkout configuration: an unfetched tag list silently selects a different window and therefore a different debt denominator, with every printed line true. Both carry the same polarity as the original defect — the cheaper the evidence is to lose, the greener the gate looks.

## What this critique is not

- Not a re-litigation of hybrid, of (a) versus (b), of the #4713 fence, of `app-claimed-origin` report-only, of the reverse index, or of the choice of `restIssueListPaginated`. C1 and C2 touch held text only to say which clause the fold must *qualify or carve out*, and both name the recording move rather than a redesign.
- Not a claim that either pain is wrong about the defect it names. Both are warranted and both close something real; the findings are about where each stops.
- Not a claim that #4713 is fixed, absorbed, or should be reopened. Facet `none` stays report-only in everything above, and C3 is in part a finding *because* it stays report-only.
- Not a softening of scoped `completed-tracked` fail-closed.
- Not a retraction call, not a halt call, not a same-fingerprint finding, and not a recommendation to reopen the held Recut's enumerator choice.
- Not an ingest claim, not a completed-arc or ingest-ready stamp, not a dest placement, not a body PATCH. `arc-mode: no-ingest`. No product edits.

## Summary

Both pains are warranted, and both are under-scoped in the same way: each names a real defect, prescribes the right polarity, and draws its boundary one step short of where its own failure mode lives.

`P1` buys a window-bounded PR walk and leaves the denominator walk unbounded — and that walk is the larger one, because the issues collection returns pull requests too and `excludePulls` filters them only *after* they have been paid for out of the same 10,000-row ceiling (`gh-rest.ts:701`, `:703`, `:729`, `:320-321`). It also cannot take `P1`'s remedy, since the helper carries no `sort`, `direction`, or `since` (`:280-285`, `:574-577`). So the fail-closed-forever horizon `P1` closes on one axis stays open on the other, and arrives sooner. Alongside that, the stop `P1` prescribes has no in-tree shape that distinguishes it from the silent truncate the held Reject list forbids — the generic paginator's `limit` path slices with no signal (`:734`), and the tree's only hand-rolled pulls loop silently truncates at its cap (`pr-closing-keywords/main.ts:147`) — and `P1`'s soundness parenthetical proves the break rather than the completeness of what precedes it.

`P2` inverts the right path and leaves the wider one. The two tag-list readers return one `null` for "not a repo", "git failed", "no tags fetched", and "no release tags" (`resolve-version.ts:119`, `:127`, `:139`, `:147`), and `P2`'s failure clause reaches only a fifth state beyond all four. The unfetched-tags state is the common one in CI, it produces W1's own symptom exactly, and repointing the root away from `frameworkRoot()` — the repair `P2` correctly prescribes — increases exposure to it rather than reducing it. `P2` also names a failure with no channel, into a matrix whose counts are all per-subject and whose default mode is warn.

The repairs are small and all of them sit inside the two pain texts: name which walks `P1`'s budget clause covers, state the stop as a recorded completeness proof, replace "sound because" with the ordering precondition it rests on, extend `P2`'s failure clause from the date conversion to the tag-list read, and give that failure a channel. None of them reopens the hybrid, and none of them is a builder recipe.

Process-only. No product edits, no ingest claim, no stamp. Critic exit after this single post.

## Summary

`verify:completed-tracked` enforces *"every closed **scoped** issue has tracked completed/cancelled land."* The word **scoped** is the hole. An issue with no xBRIEF origin is not scoped, so the gate skips it entirely and reports green.

Net effect: **the more work bypasses the lifecycle, the cleaner the gate looks.**

## Evidence — a whole session slipped through

2026-08-18/19, deftai/directive. Five issues filed, fixed, PR'd and merged:

| Issue | PR | Merge | xBRIEF |
|---|---|---|---|
| #3481 | #3485 | `96384229` | **none** |
| #3483 | #3488 | `b489da78` | **none** |
| #3484 | #3486 | `68341617` | **none** |
| #3487 | #3489 | `5c9ab11e` | **none** |
| #3492 | #3493 | `16076833` | **none** |

`verify:completed-tracked` verdict immediately afterwards:

```
verify:completed-tracked: all closed scoped issues have tracked completed/cancelled
on tip origin/master (scoped origins checked: 1116).
```

Green. `verify:orphan-active` likewise clean — it watches `active/` residue, and nothing was ever in `active/`.

So the #3476 invariant shipped in this very session is structurally blind to the workflow that produced this very session's merges.

## Cause

Both lifecycle gates are **origin-driven**: they enumerate xBRIEF artifacts, extract issue references, and check those. An issue with no artifact contributes no origin and is therefore never a subject. The gates answer *"is every brief's issue landed?"* — not *"does every landed issue have a brief?"*

Those are different questions and only the first is currently asked.

## Why it happened here (process context, not an excuse for the gap)

The operator dispatched implementation leaves using an envelope derived from `core-ops.md` STEP 1-6. That is the **leaf** envelope — leaves do not create briefs; the parent creates them in the swarm skill's earlier phases. Acting as parent while running only the leaf-facing half produces exactly this: correct code, correct PRs, no lifecycle artifacts, and no signal that anything was missing.

The relevant point for this issue is the last clause: **nothing warned.** Five times.

## Proposed change — detection, not enforcement

Add the inverse check: **a closed issue whose closing PR is merged, with no xBRIEF origin in any lifecycle folder, is reported.**

Design questions that are the substance of this issue:

1. **What is legitimately unscoped?** Dependabot bumps, trivial chores, docs typos, and revert commits should not each demand a brief. Without a defensible carve-out this becomes noise and gets ignored — which is worse than not shipping it. Candidate axes: label-based (`dependencies`), author-based (bots), or size/type-based.
2. **Warn or fail?** Suggest warn-only first with a real signal count, mirroring how `verify:telemetry-coverage` shipped warn-first with an `--enforce` flag. Fail-closed on day one would block every consumer with historical unscoped work.
3. **What window?** Scanning all history is expensive and mostly archaeology. A bounded window (since last release tag, or N days) makes it actionable.
4. **Where does it run?** It should NOT go on `task check` — that is the #1704 chokepoint and this is not a per-commit concern. A standalone verb like `verify:completed-tracked` is the right shape, callable at cohort close and release pre-flight.

## Acceptance

- A closed issue with a merged closing PR and no xBRIEF origin is reported by name.
- Legitimately unscoped classes are excluded by a stated, testable rule — not by silence.
- The five issues in the table above are detected when run against this session's range.
- Warn-only by default; `--enforce` available.

## Notes

Complements #3476 / #3264 rather than replacing them: those ensure a brief's land is tracked; this ensures landed work has a brief. Retro-briefs for the five above are being backfilled separately, so a future run of this detector should find them clean — the detector must be validated against the pre-backfill range, not after.

Refs #3476, #3264, #1358, #2321, #3479
